newsitem.title: INDIA: India's prime minister anguished by haj tragedy.
newsitem.headline: India's prime minister anguished by haj tragedy.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Wednesday that he was deeply aggrieved by the blaze in Saudi Arabia that killed more than 200 Moslem pilgrims, many of them Indians.

"The prime minister has expressed deep grief and anguish over...the devastating fire in which a large number of pilgrims from India and other countries lost their lives," said a statement from the prime minister's office.

More than 200 Moslem pilgrims were killed in the fire, triggered by a cooking gas cylinder and fanned by high winds, which swept through a sea of tents near the holy city of Mecca on Tuesday. Most of the victims were reported to be from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. They were among some two million Moslems from 100 countries gathering for the annual haj pilgrimage, which reaches its climax on Wednesday.
India's ambassador in Riyadh, Mohammad Hamad Ansari, said on Tuesday that more than 100 Indian pilgrims were believed to have died.

In New Delhi, a Foreign Ministry official in charge of an emergency haj unit set up to handle enquiries said two tents sheltering Indians were gutted in the fire but no figure for the number of Indians who were killed was yet available.
"We are trying to figure out the extent of damage and casualties," the official added.
Moslems account for nearly 12 percent of India's population of 936 million.
